Transportation Emissions

Air pollution caused by emissions from vehicles such as cars, trucks, buses, motorcycles, and, where relevant, ships or planes. Includes both exhaust and resuspended road dust due to traffic.

Keywords: vehicle emissions, traffic emissions, car exhaust, truck emissions, bus emissions, motorcycle emissions, road traffic, transportation pollution, vehicle pollution, road dust, resuspended dust, ship emissions, plane emissions, automobile pollution, urban traffic
Examples: Minister Anutin noted that private sector employees working from home will mean fewer vehicles on the road and reduced emissions and air pollution.; launch of electric buses in the capital to help improve overall air quality.; restricting the number and duration of trucks entering urban areas

Industrial and Power Plant Emissions

Air pollution resulting from emissions from factories, manufacturing facilities, industrial fuel combustion, coal-fired power plants, and mining operations. Includes sources outside city boundaries if they impact urban air quality.

Keywords: industrial emissions, factory emissions, manufacturing emissions, power plant emissions, coal-fired power plant, fossil-fueled generation, industrial pollution, mining emissions, industrial combustion, cement plant emissions, steel plant emissions
Examples: the Ministry of Industry and the Ministry of Agriculture and Cooperatives will work together in enforcing a zero-burning policy in farming zones; emissions from factories and power plants; industrial fuel combustion

Biomass Burning and Agriculture

Air pollution caused by burning of biomass for land clearing, slash-and-burn agriculture, deforestation, and wildfires. Includes cross-border and rural burning that impacts urban air quality.

Keywords: biomass burning, agricultural burning, slash-and-burn, crop burning, forest fires, wildfires, land clearing fires, deforestation burning, open burning, burning activities, zero-burning policy, hotspots, burning of sugar cane, field burning
Examples: the number of hotspots in the country increased to 56,439 points nationwide, with 31,719 in the North, of which 80% were in forest land and 15% in farming zones.; the NEB has proposed a zero-burning policy in both forest and agricultural zones; the primary source of PM2.5 in Bangkok is burning activities outside the city.

Household Emissions

Air pollution from household use of fossil fuels or biomass for cooking and heating. More relevant in rural or under-resourced settings, but included if mentioned nationally.

Keywords: household emissions, cooking smoke, biomass stoves, wood burning, charcoal burning, domestic fuel use, home heating, household air pollution, indoor air pollution, residential emissions
Examples: air pollution from household use of fossil fuels or biomass for cooking and heating; household emissions from cooking smoke; indoor air pollution from wood burning

Waste Management and Burning

Air pollution resulting from the open burning of waste, including municipal solid waste, landfill fires, and neighborhood trash burning. Only applies when combustion is explicitly mentioned.

Keywords: waste burning, open burning of waste, landfill fires, trash burning, garbage burning, municipal waste burning, refuse burning, unmanaged waste combustion, solid waste burning
Examples: air pollution from burning of waste; landfill fires contribute to air pollution; open burning of municipal solid waste

Construction and Dust

Air pollution caused by construction activities, roadworks, and resuspended soil or dust, especially during dry seasons.

Keywords: construction dust, road dust, resuspended dust, construction activities, roadworks, building sites, urban dust, soil dust, dust pollution, demolition dust
Examples: air pollution caused by construction activities; road dust resuspension due to traffic; dust pollution from building sites
